full_judgment: 9. Perused the material on record. The plaintiffs produced the deed on sale dated 6-5-1959 (Exhibit-1). They also produced the Registered Ekrarnama executed by the predecessor of the defendants (Exhibit-2), It appears from the said Ekrarnama that it was executed on the same date, written by the same scribe and attested by same witnesses and further it appears that no specific date of repayment of consideration money was mentioned in the said deed. The Ekrarnama (Exhibit- 2) is a registered deed carrying usual presumption of its validity. In support of the execution of the aforesaid Ekrarnama besides PW 1 (plaintiff No.1) PW 2 Md Yaseen was also examined who deposed that he was present at the time of execution of the aforesaid Ekrarnama. There is nothing in the cross-examination of this witness to disbelieve him nor there is any enmity between this witness and the defendants and there is no suggestion even to this witness of any enmity and, as such, I have no reason to disbelieve the claim of genuineness of the Ekrarnama on the basis of evidence produced in this behalf. The defence version is that by misleading the predecessor of the defendants namely, Jamir Hossain the deed was obtained from him. I have considered evidence of DWs in this connection. The defendant failed to point out any material to indicate that he was either illiterate or otherwise simpleton man. On the contrary, it appears that he was serving as a clerk in the police office and was sufficiently educated man and, as such, the story of obtaining the deed, registered duly, from the aforesaid predecessor of the defendants by misleading him cannot be believed. The trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court, on the basis of the evidence, found the document to be genuine. There is no misreading or non consideration of any evidence and, as such, I do not find any reason to differ with such concurrent finding of fact.
